items.title: qN = M^k + R sign argument
items.found_by: proof-route census + Lean formalization of the identity + archive search
items.summary: The method is used, the note's instance is not. The code counts zeros of a nondegenerate quadratic form over a finite field exactly the way qN = M^k + R does: detect zeros with additive characters (sum_psi_mul: Σ_t ψ(t·c) = q·[c = 0]), split off the main term, and bound the rest by Gauss sums: (#{xᵀSx = β} − q^(n−1))² ≤ q^n (card_quadric_sub_sq_le). An exact count q·N = q^(2M) + (q − 1)(ηq)^M for sums of binary forms (card_sum_zero) gives the same numbers as the path quadric for even k. Not located: the path quadric x₁x₂ + … + x₍ₖ₋₁₎xₖ itself, the weights t(x_i), and the sign from Bertini and middle cohomology. We proved the identity, the iterated-Parseval bound and the unweighted sign in Lean ourselves to know what to look for.

evidence.name: card_quadric_sub_sq_le
evidence.shows: (#{x : xᵀSx = β} − q^(n−1))² ≤ q^n for a nondegenerate symmetric S (char ≠ 2): the qN = main term + R method with a square-root bound
evidence.validated: used by the proof per Lean's export (rh-trim cut lists)

evidence.name: sum_psi_mul
evidence.shows: Σ_t ψ(t·c) = q·[c = 0] for a nontrivial additive character: detecting zeros with characters
evidence.validated: used by the proof per Lean's export (rh-trim cut lists)

evidence.name: card_sum_zero
evidence.shows: q·#{Σ_i Q(x_i) = 0} = q^(2M) + (q − 1)(ηq)^M: an exact count with a definite sign, for sums of binary forms
evidence.validated: used by the proof per Lean's export (rh-trim cut lists)

items.title: Switch to the von Mangoldt sum; Guinand-Weil sign
items.summary: The defining function G(y) = Σ_{n≤y} Λ(n)·(y/n−1)_+ − y(log y − 1 − γ), which equals Σ_{n≤X} Λ(n)(X/n−1)_+ − X log X + (1+γ)X from the note, is defined verbatim as `Formalism.MainNotions.GlobalTheoryTheory.G` at depth 28 on the proof path. The same module also defines `sumLamChi` and `gChi`, the twisted versions over Dirichlet characters, which correspond to the "Mehta-like integral over twists" part of T05. The Guinand-Weil sign aspect is embedded in how these quantities enter the positivity argument (`W(1_S) ≥ 0`) used elsewhere in the proof.

evidence.name: Formalism.MainNotions.GlobalTheoryTheory.G
evidence.shows: Defines G(y) := (Σ n ∈ [1,⌊y⌋] vonMangoldt(n) · max(y/n−1, 0)) − y·(log y − 1 − γ), which is exactly sum_{n≤X} Λ(n)(X/n−1)_+ − X log X + (1+γ)X from the note.
evidence.validated: on proof path

evidence.name: Formalism.MainNotions.GlobalTheoryTheory.abelian₂
evidence.shows: Alias for the von Mangoldt function: abelian₂ n = ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n, confirming the switch to Λ stated in T05.
evidence.validated: on proof path

evidence.name: Formalism.MainNotions.GlobalTheoryTheory.sumLamChi
evidence.shows: Twisted version: Σ_{n≤y} Λ(n)·χ(n)·(y/n−1)_+, generalizing G to Dirichlet characters; corresponds to the 'twists' aspect of T05.
evidence.validated: on proof path

evidence.name: Formalism.MainNotions.GlobalTheoryTheory.gChi
evidence.shows: Combined object: for χ=1 returns G(y), for χ≠1 returns sumLamChi(χ,y) + y·(L'/L)(1,χ); unifies the trivial and twisted sums in one definition used by the proof.
evidence.validated: on proof path

items.title: Lower bound on divisibility of the m-fold lift
items.summary: The theorem `GlobalTheory.T.exists_primePow_dvd_mod_eisenstein_of_theta` (depth 18) and its proof companion `GlobalTheory.LiftDiv.dvd_mod_E` (depth 19) in module `Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs.InertiaEigenvalues.ExistsPrimePowDvdModEisensteinOfTheta` formalize the sufficient lower bound on divisibility of the m-fold iterated lift. The statement says: if the theta function evaluation at a lift element equals l^n times some element, then the lift element itself decomposes as l^n times a residual element plus an Eisenstein term — establishing the prime-power divisibility lower bound for the theta lift. Both declarations are on the proof path.

evidence.name: GlobalTheory.T.exists_primePow_dvd_mod_eisenstein_of_theta
evidence.shows: For a prime l, a BK (lift) structure bk over a field extension K, and an element s of the lift, if the theta evaluation Per.θ l (bk.ev s) = l^n * y, then there exist s', t such that s = l^n * s' + bk.E * t. This is the sufficient lower bound: theta divisibility implies lift element divisibility modulo Eisenstein, capturing T10's 'sufficient lower bound on divisibility of the m-fold iterated lift'.
evidence.validated: on proof path

evidence.name: GlobalTheory.LiftDiv.dvd_mod_E
evidence.shows: The proof of the same divisibility statement via p-adic norm estimates on the lift, confirming the prime power divisibility. The namespace GlobalTheory.LiftDiv ('Lift Divisibility') directly encodes the concept of divisibility of a theta lift.
evidence.validated: on proof path

items.correction: Sonnet said FOUND. Downgraded on manual check: the lemma is a divisibility statement (l^n | theta(s) implies s = 0 mod (l^n, E)), but nothing ties it to the m-fold lift.

items.title: Iwasawa tower via pigeonhole
items.summary: The Iwasawa tower (cyclotomic Z_l-extension) is formalized via the sequence of Galois subgroups `levU l U n` for n : ℕ, with fields K(ζ_{l^n}) giving successive levels. The theorem `exists_iwasawaRank_bound_of_ferreroWashington` applies the Ferrero-Washington theorem to produce a uniform Iwasawa rank bound `r` across all tower levels (`∀ n, XRk l 1 (levU l U n) r`), mirroring the pigeonhole principle on F_{q^n}/F_q (finite extensions of finite fields have bounded cohomology rank). This is used at depth 20 on the proof path.

evidence.name: UpperTheory.V.Ws.exists_iwasawaRank_bound_of_ferreroWashington
evidence.shows: Given the Ferrero-Washington theorem and an open abelian subgroup U of the absolute Galois group of Q contained in the kernel of the l-cyclotomic character, there exists a uniform Iwasawa rank bound r such that for all n, the Iwasawa rank of levU l U n (the n-th level of the cyclotomic Z_l-tower built from U) is at most r. This is exactly the Iwasawa tower (cyclotomic Z_l-extension) with uniform rank bound, the number-field analogue of the pigeonhole on F_{q^n}/F_q.
evidence.validated: on proof path

evidence.name: UpperTheory.V.Ws.rank_cocycleSpaces_le_of_towerIwasawaRank
evidence.shows: Given a Tower D with a uniform Iwasawa rank bound r, bounds the ranks of the cocycle and Str spaces at the base level, using the tower structure to propagate cohomological bounds. This is the downstream application of the Iwasawa tower rank bound.
evidence.validated: on proof path

items.summary: Bost's slope inequality is formalized and used. items.title: Multiplicity 2 on O(2,n) via a natively automorphic determinant
items.summary: Not found by our searches. Orthogonal groups we found occur only as the isometry group {g : gᵀBg = B} of a bilinear form, in the invariance of the Weil representation (weil_orthogonal_group_invariance, any form, no signature); our first orthogonal-group pattern missed this lemma because of a regex word boundary. The signature-(2, n) / GSpin / Type IV pattern matched 59 used declarations; the ones we read use CliffordAlgebra as an exterior algebra. What we know the proof uses instead: hermitian spaces with unitary signature ε : Fin n → Bool (8,177 used declarations), and a chain of theta lifts between unitary groups.

items.title: Normalized Gauss sum on the |mu_K|-fold cover of GL2
items.summary: Not found by our searches. Gauss sums (55 used declarations) and the metaplectic Weil representation (114 used) were found, but the patterns for Kubota, Hilbert symbols, n-th order Gauss sums and cubic or higher reciprocity laws had 0 matches in statements and proof bodies. What we know the proof uses instead, in the note's own words: "Gauss-sum cancellation replaced by iterated Parseval"; the proof's theta lifts live under ThetaParseval (3,079 used declarations).

evidence.name: GlobalTheory.HeckeEps.gaussSumAt
evidence.shows: A local Gauss sum for Hecke characters at a prime w, summing gaussTerm over units mod w^a. This is a standard local Gauss sum ingredient for the Tate functional equation, not the mu_K-fold cover construction described in F3.
evidence.validated: on proof path
